global.headline: LAVROV LANDS IN TEHRAN OFFERING TO TAKE IRAN'S URANIUM WHILE FIFTEEN CONTAINER SHIPS BURN IN THE STRAIT
summary: Iran has struck at least 15 container ships in the Strait of Hormuz in ten days — by drone, by mine, and on Sunday by a rocket-propelled grenade fired from a small boat off Jubail. UKMTO logged 254 transits in the week to 14 October, about 70 per cent below pre-conflict levels; Brent traded near US$108 on Monday. Boatmen have been cutting open containers spilt from the Singapore-flagged GFS Pride, which sank on 14 October after hitting a mine, all 21 crew evacuated; the IRGC told fishers the cargo is state property and repeated that it may attack any ship crossing without its permission.

Sergei Lavrov arrived in Tehran offering Russia as intermediary between Iran and Donald Trump, proposing that Moscow take custody of Iran's highly enriched uranium and convening a China-Russia-Iran summit on a new security architecture for the strait; he said the region is on the verge of full-scale crisis. Iran has barred IAEA inspectors from its bombed nuclear sites since June 2025 and will not commit on the programme, and its price for reopening the strait in six days is unchanged. Netanyahu launched a new Israeli security doctrine on Sunday built on pre-emptive strikes.
global.geopolitical: Moscow is moving to occupy the two roles Washington has refused — custodian of Iran's fissile material and broker of the waterway — three days after the White House waived the sanctions law written against Russia. If Tehran accepts, reopening the strait becomes something the United States must ask Russia for.
global.socioeconomic: A 70 per cent collapse in transits is the figure that matters: the strait is functionally shut to anyone without IRGC clearance, and the premium is now embedded in every cargo insurance quote and every barrel priced off Brent.

global.headline: THREE MISSILES HIT A YEMENI TRAINING CAMP AND KILL 53 RECRUITS, AND RIYADH CALLS OFF DAVOS IN THE DESERT
summary: Three Houthi ballistic missiles struck al-Alam camp in government-held Shabwa province while recruits stood in formation, killing at least 53 and injuring more than 200 — the largest single loss of life since Yemen's war reignited in September. President Rashad al-Alimi promised an immediate hard response and asked Antonio Guterres to have the UN designate the Houthis a foreign terrorist organisation. The Houthi spokesman said the camp was run by Saudi officers who were among the dead, offering no evidence; the government called it an internal security training centre far from the front and opened an inquiry into why so many troops were massed within missile range. A Saudi airstrike on Sunday killed nine, five of them children.

The FII Institute postponed the tenth Future Investment Initiative, due in Riyadh from 26 to 29 October, to 2027; the decision follows the 10 October strike on King Khalid International Airport and joins Riyadh Fashion Week and an EU-Gulf summit among cancelled events. Egypt's parliament extended its Article 152 debate to a second day and then deferred the vote again, now likely next week, with opposition parties signalling abstention and members disputing whether Egyptian troops would enter Yemen or only stand inside Saudi Arabia.
global.geopolitical: Cairo's second deferral measures the coalition Riyadh is trying to assemble: Egypt will not commit two-thirds of its House to a mission whose size and location nobody has stated, and the delay waits on both Iranian restraint of the Houthis and the renewal of Saudi loans to Egypt.
global.socioeconomic: Losing the FII shuts Vision 2030's shop window in the year the kingdom most needs foreign capital — the conference exists to sell Saudi Arabia as investable, and it was cancelled precisely because it no longer is.

global.headline: PARIS GETS ITS FIRST CURFEW AFTER THE INTERIOR MINISTER CONCEDES THE POLICE LOST CONTROL
summary: France imposed partial curfews on Monday: 11pm to 6am around Place de la Republique and Les Halles in Paris, and 8pm to 6am on Monday and Tuesday nights in four northern cities including Lille. Marseille banned all gatherings. Sebastien Lecornu said after an emergency cabinet meeting that he was "fully resolved to restore public order" but that there was "no question" of curfewing whole cities, a state of emergency remaining possible though less appropriate.

Interior minister Laurent Nunez conceded a "lack of anticipation": intelligence forecast 200,000 demonstrators, more than 500,000 came, and 60,000 deployed officers were overwhelmed. "You couldn't look shopkeepers in the eye after hundreds of shops had been looted and say we hadn't lost control." He offered his resignation; Macron refused it and ordered transparency over the intelligence failure and new operational methods. Justice minister Gerald Darmanin put arrests at 2,513 with 67 jailed and about 80 per cent being prosecuted; almost 1,000 police and gendarmes have been injured and some 2,000 shops ransacked. The digital minister summoned Vinted, eBay, Amazon, Meta and TikTok over listings of looted goods; protesters blocked the Louvre, which could not open; unions called fresh strikes for 5 November. Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said "it is the state that was at fault" and Marseille's Benoit Payan called the situation "almost insurrectional".
global.geopolitical: Six months from a presidential election a government that has conceded its police lost control has handed the National Rally its argument intact, while Trump's intervention — "migrants have taken over France" — attaches an immigration frame to a revolt French officials attribute to living costs and school conditions.
global.socioeconomic: Two thousand looted shops and a curfew over the capital's main retail district fall on small traders with no insurance margin, and the 5 November strike call gives the disruption a fixed date to build towards rather than a weekend to burn out in.

global.headline: ZELENSKY SAYS WASHINGTON IS STEERING HIM TOWARDS CAPITULATION AS A THIRD EUROPEAN STARLINK SITE IS SET ALIGHT
summary: Zelensky told Bloomberg that steps were being taken to push Ukraine towards capitulation, saying he did not want to believe Washington wanted the war ended at Ukraine's expense "but that's how it looks". Trump had posted on Sunday night that Zelensky "doesn't want to end this war, and probably never did", and said on Monday that somebody else should negotiate for Ukraine. Zelensky put American Patriot deliveries at about 12 interceptors a month, roughly a quarter of the previous administration's rate, and said he had been willing to halt refinery strikes in exchange for more. Richard Blumenthal, after a senators' call, said Zelensky told them Ukraine still lacks full access to both Starshield and US intelligence sharing — two days after Zelensky said publicly the feed had been restored. Adviser Serhii Beskrestnov told the BBC Ukrainians are dying because there is no longer time to warn them of incoming missiles; the White House says nothing has changed.

Lithuania said an attempted arson at a Starlink base station outside Vilnius early Sunday was Russia-linked sabotage. Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius said the company had been warned, the attempt failed with minor damage and no loss of service, and investigators know who was responsible. It is the third such site hit in Europe, after antennas burned in Bulgaria on 10 October and a Polish facility's power system in September. Moscow calls the accusations baseless.
global.geopolitical: The same network is being degraded from Washington by policy and from Moscow by arson, leaving Kyiv unable to treat either as an outage it can plan around — and giving Russia reason to keep testing how far the sabotage goes unanswered.
global.socioeconomic: Twelve interceptors a month against nightly ballistic salvoes is arithmetic, not a dispute: it sets how much of Ukraine's generating capacity survives to December, and therefore how many more people leave.

global.headline: A KENYAN COURT CONVICTS A PASTOR OF 191 MURDERS, ALL BUT ONE OF THEM CHILDREN
summary: The High Court in Mombasa found Paul Nthenge Mackenzie and 28 co-accused guilty on 191 counts of murder over the Shakahola forest starvation deaths, 190 of the victims children. Justice Diana Kavedza-Mochache read the judgment for more than nine hours, holding that the prosecution — 121 witnesses, postmortems and government analyst findings — had proved its case against all 29, and rejecting the defence that the dead had fasted willingly to meet Jesus. Hundreds of bodies were exhumed after the sect was uncovered. Sentencing is set for 6 November; Mackenzie's lawyer called the verdict perplexing and will appeal.
global.geopolitical: The ruling establishes that a religious leader can be convicted of murder for deaths he ordered rather than carried out — the precedent Kenya's stalled attempts to regulate churches have lacked, in a country where religious bodies have resisted registration rules for years.
global.socioeconomic: It is a child-protection failure before it is a criminal case: 190 children starved over months inside a known settlement, and the state's answer so far is a conviction rather than any mechanism that would have found them earlier.

singapore.headline: THE WAGES COUNCIL ASKS FOR 6 TO 8 PER CENT FOR THE LOWEST PAID, ITS BIGGEST NUMBER SINCE 2021
summary: The National Wages Council recommended built-in increases of 6 to 8 per cent for workers earning up to S$2,800 a month — the highest since quantitative guidelines for lower-wage workers began in 2021 — and the government accepted them on Monday. They run from 1 December 2026 to 30 November 2027 and take a "positive-leaning approach" after stronger-than-expected growth. Employers doing well with positive prospects should pay at the top of the range or at least S$135 to S$170, whichever is higher; those facing uncertainty around the middle; profitable underperformers at the bottom or at least S$120; and a new fourth tier asks unprofitable firms for at least S$120. MOM permanent secretary Stanley Loh said slightly more than a quarter of employers met last year's recommendation, down from over 70 per cent before the 2021 expansion widened the covered group, though more than 60 per cent of those who fell short still raised wages.
singapore.geopolitical: A wage floor set by tripartite recommendation rather than legislation works only if employers follow it, and an adoption rate of just over a quarter is the model's weakest reading in years.
singapore.socioeconomic: Six to eight per cent on a S$2,800 ceiling is a real gain against headline inflation near 1.8 per cent, but it will be judged on whether the new unprofitable-firm tier becomes the default answer.

singapore.headline: THE HAZE LIST REACHES TEN COMPANIES AND THE EXCHANGE STARTS ASKING SEVEN LISTED FIRMS WHAT THEY BOUGHT
summary: NEA issued preventive measure notices to three more Indonesian companies — PT Buana Megatama Jaya, PT Mananjung Hayak and PT Baratama Putra Perkasa — after indications that smoke from fires on Kalimantan land under their concessions reached Singapore, taking to ten the companies targeted under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act. The notices are not a finding of legal responsibility. K Shanmugam said firms "cannot play hide and seek" and that if they refuse to cooperate, whether or not they have a presence here, the government will use "every legal and regulatory lever at its disposal"; he called the smog entirely preventable and said Singapore appreciates the Prabowo administration's efforts. He named Asia Pulp and Paper as a buyer from three companies already served, and said hotspots also appeared associated with listed First Resources and Bumitama Agri, and with First Borneo Plantations. The exchange separately queried seven listed agricultural companies — Golden Agri-Resources, Bumitama Agri, First Resources, Wilmar, Kencana Agri, Indofood Agri and TSH Resources. Air quality improved overnight, three of five regions reading moderate PSI by Tuesday morning, and Firefly plans to resume all Subang-Seletar flights on 22 October.
singapore.geopolitical: Moving from unnamed concession holders to named listed buyers shifts the instrument from the 2014 Act, which needs Indonesian causation evidence Singapore cannot compel, to disclosure rules the exchange enforces here without Jakarta's cooperation.
singapore.socioeconomic: Pulling seven listed names into a supply-chain inquiry puts their financing and index standing in question before any liability is established — which is the point: the cost lands on buyers who can price it back down the chain.

singapore.headline: SINGAPORE AND QATAR AGREE TO UPGRADE TO A STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP AND RENEW THE LNG MEMORANDUM
summary: In Doha on the first Middle East trip of his premiership, Lawrence Wong and Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani agreed to work towards raising relations to a strategic partnership, which would make Qatar Singapore's second such partner in the region. They oversaw renewal of a memorandum between QatarEnergy and the Ministry of Trade and Industry on LNG and low-carbon technology; Qatar supplies about a quarter of Singapore's LNG imports. The ninth High-Level Joint Committee met the same day, the first time in its 20 years that both leaders co-chaired it. Wong met Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani on Sunday on energy security, supply chains and AI, and flies to the UAE on Tuesday.
singapore.geopolitical: Singapore is deepening ties with the two Gulf states still functioning as reliable counterparties while a standing advisory tells its citizens to defer all travel to Saudi Arabia — a quiet sorting of the Gulf into states the war has reached and states it has not.
singapore.socioeconomic: A quarter of the island's LNG comes from one supplier in a war zone, so renewing the procurement memorandum is electricity policy: it is the contract behind the tariff, which fell 10.4 per cent this quarter from a record high.

singapore.headline: THREE THOUSAND YEAR-LONG INTERNSHIPS BECAUSE AI HAS TAKEN THE JUNIOR ENGINEER'S FIRST JOB
summary: Senior Minister of State Tan Kiat How announced at the Singapore Computer Society's TechConnect that about 3,000 year-long internships will be offered to tertiary students over three years as AI reshapes entry-level technology work. The credit-bearing placements run 10 to 12 months within the curriculum and extend IMDA's Bridge2Tech and TIP Alliance+ schemes, which have covered ITE and polytechnic students since 2022, to the autonomous universities for the first time. Students can draw IMDA funding for up to 90 per cent of approved courses in AI, cloud and cybersecurity. Tan said junior engineers once learned by writing simpler programmes, debugging, testing and maintaining systems — tasks AI now largely handles.
singapore.geopolitical: Singapore is treating the disappearance of entry-level technology work as a structural problem needing a public instrument, rather than a labour-market statistic to be monitored.
singapore.socioeconomic: A year-long placement is a wage subsidy in all but name, and 3,000 places over three years is small against annual cohorts — the test is whether firms that stopped hiring juniors restart, not the headcount.

word.definition: The breakdown of the shared norms that bind a society, leaving individuals without effective moral restraint or sense of belonging.
word.etymology: From Greek anomia, lawlessness — a-, without, plus nomos, law. Borrowed into French as anomie and given its modern sociological sense by Emile Durkheim in 1893 for the normlessness that follows rapid social change.
word.example: When Marseille's mayor called the weekend "almost insurrectional" and Paris's said the state itself was at fault, they were describing anomie rather than crime: 2,000 shops looted by people who no longer expected anyone to stop them.
